title: Understanding the Logistic Regression Model
text: In logistic regression, the probability of an event is modeled using the logistic function, which is defined as \( \sigma(z) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-z}} \). The value of \( $$z$$ \) is calculated as a linear combination of the input features and their corresponding coefficients.

title: Calculate the Linear Combination
text: To find the value of \( $$z$$ \), use the formula \( $$z$$ $$=$$ \beta_0 + \beta_1 \times \text{age} + \beta_2 \times \text{sex} \). Substitute the given values: \( \beta_0 $$=$$ $$-1.2$$ \), \( \beta_1 $$=$$ $$-0.005$$ \), \( \beta_2 $$=$$ $$2.5$$ \), \( \text{age} $$=$$ $$20$$ \), and \( \text{sex} $$=$$ $$1$$ \) for female.

title: Substitute the Values
text: Substitute the values into the equation: \( $$z$$ $$=$$ $$-1.2$$ + $$(-0.005)$$ \times $$20$$ + $$2.5$$ \times $$1$$ \). Calculate \( $$z$$ \).

title: Calculate the Probability
text: Once you have the value of \( $$z$$ \), use the logistic function \( \sigma(z) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-z}} \) to calculate the probability of survival.

title: Final Probability
text: Using the logistic function, calculate the probability: \( $$\sigma(1.2)$$ \).
